content.value_statement: Medical device teams must interpret EU MDR rules across classification, evidence, documentation, and surveillance. This skill helps structure compliance work and prepare regulatory decisions.
actual_capabilities: Guides device classification under MDR Annex VIII and conformity assessment route selection.
Outlines Annex II and Annex III technical documentation structure.
Helps plan clinical evidence, clinical investigations, and PMCF activities.
Maps post-market surveillance duties, PSUR needs, incident reporting, and trend reporting.
Supports Notified Body selection criteria and audit preparation planning.
limitations: It does not replace legal advice, Notified Body feedback, or competent authority decisions.
It cannot verify live MDR guidance updates unless connected to current sources.
It requires accurate device details, intended purpose, and market context.
It does not certify devices or submit records to EUDAMED.

use_cases.title: Classify a medical device
use_cases.description: Assess intended purpose, duration, invasiveness, and software function against MDR Annex VIII rules.

use_cases.title: Prepare technical documentation
use_cases.description: Organize Annex II and Annex III evidence, labeling, risk management, and validation materials.

use_cases.title: Plan clinical evidence work
use_cases.description: Identify clinical evaluation, investigation, and PMCF needs for a device or portfolio.

prompt_templates.title: Classify My Device
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify this device under EU MDR Annex VIII. Intended purpose: [describe]. Duration: [transient, short-term, or long-term]. Invasiveness: [describe]. Software role: [describe]. Explain the likely class and key assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Technical File Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an MDR Annex II and Annex III technical documentation outline for this device: [device details]. Include required evidence sections, owners, and open information gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Clinical Evidence Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this clinical evidence summary for MDR readiness: [paste summary]. Identify gaps, likely PMCF needs, and questions for the clinical evaluation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Create an MDR Transition Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an MDR transition roadmap for this device portfolio: [portfolio details]. Include classification risks, technical documentation gaps, clinical evidence priorities, PMS updates, Notified Body dependencies, and milestones.

output_examples.input: A manufacturer asks how to classify reusable surgical instruments under MDR.
output: Likely classification: Class I reusable surgical instrument, subject to Notified Body involvement for reusable aspects.
Key evidence: intended purpose, reuse process validation, cleaning validation, labeling, and risk management documentation.
Next step: confirm whether any active, invasive, measuring, or sterile characteristics change the route.

output_examples.input: A quality team needs a post-market surveillance plan for a Class IIb device.
output: Recommended structure: PMS objectives, data sources, complaint handling, vigilance, trend reporting, PSUR schedule, and PMCF linkage.
Priority gap: define signal thresholds and responsibilities for escalation to competent authorities.
Review point: align PMS outputs with risk management and clinical evaluation updates.

output_examples.input: A startup wants to prepare for a Notified Body submission.
output: Readiness focus: classification rationale, complete technical documentation, QMS evidence, clinical evaluation, and PMS process records.
Selection criteria: device scope, capacity, certificate timelines, fee model, and experience with similar technologies.
Submission risk: unresolved clinical evidence gaps may delay review.

best_practices: Provide intended purpose, patient population, duration, invasiveness, and software role before classification.
Cross-reference each recommendation with MDR articles, annexes, and current MDCG guidance.
Treat outputs as planning support and confirm critical decisions with qualified regulatory counsel.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to bypass Notified Body review or authority requirements.
Do not assume legacy directive files satisfy MDR documentation expectations.
Do not omit adverse event, complaint, or PMCF data from surveillance planning.

faq.question: What regulation does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on EU MDR 2017/745 for medical devices placed on the European Union market.

faq.question: Can it determine the final legal device class?
faq.answer: It can support classification analysis, but final decisions should be confirmed by qualified regulatory experts or authorities.

faq.question: Does it help with technical documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines Annex II and Annex III documentation needs and helps identify missing evidence.

faq.question: Can it prepare clinical evaluation work?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps plan clinical evidence, clinical investigation needs, and PMCF activities.

faq.question: Does it submit information to EUDAMED?
faq.answer: No. It can explain UDI and EUDAMED preparation needs, but it does not submit records.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Regulatory, quality, and clinical teams can use it for MDR planning, gap analysis, and submission preparation.
